title: Initial external Design System reference adapter
question: Which external Design System foundation best supports Meridian's first exchangeable reference adapter for SaaS, administration, and business-tool UI generation?

scope.summary: Compare external React-oriented foundations without making any candidate the Meridian source of truth.

constraints: Project-existing Design Systems remain higher priority than the selected default adapter.
The Capability Plan must not contain vendor component names.
The initial adapter must not become the Meridian design source of truth.
A final recommendation requires Team Invitation and Issue Triage comparative spikes.

criteria.name: Accessibility and keyboard behavior
criteria.description: Native semantics, WAI-ARIA behavior, focus management, keyboard interaction, and assistive-technology evidence.

criteria.name: SaaS and administration component coverage
criteria.description: Coverage of forms, overlays, navigation, collections, tables, and business application states.

criteria.name: AI readability and generation safety
criteria.description: Availability of inspectable source, schemas, registries, predictable APIs, and provenance-friendly distribution.

criteria.name: Token and theme portability
criteria.description: Ability to map project or DTCG semantic tokens without making vendor styling the source of truth.

criteria.name: Capability Adapter fit
criteria.description: Ability to resolve a vendor-neutral Capability Plan into versioned component usage and report unsupported capabilities.

criteria.name: Internationalization and RTL
criteria.description: Locale-sensitive behavior, RTL support, input modality support, and long-content resilience.

criteria.name: Data-intensive UI capability
criteria.description: Support for comparison, selection, sorting, row actions, high density, and large collections.

criteria.name: License and vendor lock-in
criteria.description: License clarity, paid feature boundaries, source ownership, migration cost, and dependency concentration.

criteria.name: Performance and delivery cost
criteria.description: Bundle, runtime, installation, update, and generated-code maintenance implications.

criteria.name: Documentation and maintenance
criteria.description: Official documentation quality, release visibility, upgrade path, and long-term maintenance signals.

criteria.name: Design tooling interoperability
criteria.description: Availability of design resources and a credible path to Figma or other design-tool integration.

candidates.name: shadcn/ui
candidates.license: MIT for the official source; installed registry items and their dependencies require item-level verification.
limitations: Open-code ownership shifts update and drift management to the consuming project.
Advanced data-grid behavior requires an additional approved composition or dependency.

candidates.name: Radix Primitives
candidates.license: MIT; exact package and version must be recorded by the adapter.
limitations: Provides accessible primitives rather than a complete visual Design System.
Does not provide a complete data-intensive application component set.

candidates.name: React Aria Components
candidates.license: Apache-2.0; exact package and version must be recorded by the adapter.
limitations: Provides behavior and accessibility without a finished visual language.
Requires Meridian-owned styling and composition work.

candidates.name: Material UI and MUI X
candidates.license: Material UI is MIT; MUI X Community is MIT while Pro and Premium features use commercial licenses.
limitations: Material visual and API conventions may increase adaptation cost for Meridian profiles.
Some advanced data capabilities require commercial MUI X plans.

candidates.name: Carbon Design System
candidates.license: Apache-2.0; exact package, Sass toolchain, font, and any community extension must be recorded by the adapter.
limitations: Carbon visual conventions and Sass integration create adaptation cost for non-Carbon project profiles.
Complete RTL and first-party large-collection virtualization support were not established by the reviewed evidence.

evidence.title: Introduction - shadcn/ui
evidence.summary: The official documentation defines shadcn/ui as an open-code component distribution approach with composable interfaces and AI-readable source.
limitations: Documentation claims require comparative implementation evidence before scoring.

evidence.title: Registry - shadcn/ui
evidence.summary: The official registry supports schema-validated distribution of components, hooks, pages, configuration, rules, and other files.
limitations: Registry compatibility does not prove UI capability or accessibility quality.

evidence.title: RTL Support - shadcn/ui
evidence.summary: The CLI converts physical utilities and directional props to logical RTL-aware output and publishes RTL examples for components.
limitations: Third-party registry items and table engines still require independent RTL verification.

evidence.title: shadcn eject
evidence.summary: CLI 4.8.3 can inline shared Tailwind utilities and remove the shadcn runtime CSS dependency, preserving project ownership of generated source.
limitations: Source ownership transfers merge, drift, and security update responsibility to the project.

evidence.title: Vite installation - shadcn/ui
evidence.summary: The official Vite integration uses React with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4 through @tailwindcss/vite, and an explicit @ alias; the parity Spike follows this build boundary with exact-pinned packages.
limitations: Successful source compilation does not by itself establish assistive-technology conformance or select shadcn as the reference adapter.

evidence.title: Introduction - Radix Primitives
evidence.summary: Radix describes an unstyled, accessible, typed, incrementally adoptable primitive layer with controlled and uncontrolled APIs.
limitations: The documentation does not establish complete SaaS component coverage.

evidence.title: Accessibility - Radix Primitives
evidence.summary: Radix documents WAI-ARIA-oriented roles, labels, keyboard navigation, and focus management for its primitives.
limitations: Meridian must still verify generated compositions in its target browser and assistive-technology matrix.

evidence.title: Radix Primitives Releases
evidence.summary: The July 2026 releases document active ARIA-reference, focus, form-event, tree-shaking, and React compatibility fixes.
limitations: Release activity does not fill missing data-collection capabilities.

evidence.title: Getting Started - React Aria
evidence.summary: React Aria provides unstyled components and hooks with accessibility, internationalization, interactions, and behavior across input modalities.
limitations: Official claims require Meridian-specific composition and browser verification.

evidence.title: react-aria-components package
evidence.summary: Version 1.19.0 exposes over 50 unstyled components with adaptive interaction, accessibility, internationalization, RTL, and Apache-2.0 licensing.
limitations: Package metadata and documentation claims do not replace candidate-specific browser evaluation.

evidence.title: Adobe React Spectrum repository
evidence.summary: The official repository documents Apache-2.0 licensing, screen-reader and device testing, adaptive input support, over 30 languages, RTL, and active releases.
limitations: Virtualization and advanced collection APIs still need pinned stability checks.

evidence.title: Material UI Overview
evidence.summary: Material UI provides a comprehensive production-oriented React component library with theming and design resources.
limitations: The overview does not measure adaptation cost to Meridian visual profiles.

evidence.title: MUI X Licensing
evidence.summary: MUI X separates MIT Community packages from commercially licensed Pro and Premium capabilities.
limitations: Pricing and feature boundaries are ecosystem-sensitive and must be rechecked before approval.

evidence.title: Material UI Localization
evidence.summary: Material UI supplies locale packs through theme configuration and documents RTL support; MUI X Data Grid has a separate localization boundary.
limitations: Material UI and Data Grid locale inputs must be synchronized by the adapter.

evidence.title: Upcoming Changes to MUI X Pricing and Licensing in 2026
evidence.summary: MUI documents 2026 Pro and Premium price changes, application-based licensing, Enterprise support boundaries, and v9 license-key changes.
limitations: Pricing and plan entitlements can change and require revalidation immediately before approval.

evidence.title: Carbon Design System repository
evidence.summary: The repository publishes Carbon under Apache-2.0 with React packages, migration guides, security policy, and active 2026 releases.
limitations: Repository activity does not prove project-specific RTL or visual adaptation quality.

evidence.title: Carbon Components Overview
evidence.summary: Carbon provides a broad enterprise component catalog including forms, overlays, navigation, status, pagination, and data tables.
limitations: Some components and community assets use feature flags or separate maturity boundaries.

evidence.title: Carbon Data Table Usage
evidence.summary: Carbon Data Table documents sorting, selection, expansion, row and batch actions, pagination, toolbar filtering, and five densities.
limitations: The reviewed guidance does not establish first-party virtualization or a narrow-viewport master-detail strategy.

evidence.title: Carbon Data Table Accessibility
evidence.summary: Carbon documents keyboard sorting, table-control operation, accessible naming, aria-sort, automated checks, and manual screen-reader testing.
limitations: Meridian must still verify the generated composition and selected version.

evidence.title: Carbon Themes
evidence.summary: Carbon exposes role-based theme tokens and Sass/CSS-variable output across White, Gray 10, Gray 90, and Gray 100 themes.
limitations: A DTCG-to-Carbon semantic map and Sass build integration remain adapter work.

evidence.title: Design Tokens Format Module 2025.10
evidence.summary: The stable community report defines a vendor-neutral interchange format for typed design tokens, aliases, and tool extensions.
limitations: Each adapter still needs an explicit mapping from DTCG semantic roles to vendor styling APIs.

spikes.title: Team Invitation comparative adapter spike
spikes.hypothesis: The same approved Team Invitation Capability Plan can be resolved through each candidate without changing Screen Responsibility or Requirement Allocation.
measurements: Desktop, Tablet, and Mobile browser findings
findings: All candidates are assessed against the same nine Team Invitation capabilities.
Responsive reflow is generator-owned instead of being falsely attributed to a component package.
Radix requires the most Meridian-owned form and collection composition; React Aria and shadcn cover the contract without a paid boundary; MUI and Carbon provide more finished visuals.

The isolated pinned implementation completed Desktop, Tablet RTL, and Mobile forced-colors automation for all five candidates with no critical or major automated finding after one responsive repair loop.
The shadcn candidate materializes all nine captured new-york-v4 registry TSX files unchanged and compiles them with the pinned Tailwind v4 Vite toolchain before the shared browser matrix.
Tablet RTL initially made narrow table columns illegible without horizontal overflow; the generator-owned responsive boundary was repaired to use the shared card presentation at 820 pixels and below.
VoiceOver, browser UI zoom, and Windows High Contrast remain manual selection blockers; automated results do not establish accessibility conformance.

spikes.title: Issue Triage comparative adapter spike
spikes.hypothesis: The candidates can support a data-intensive Master-Detail or Task Queue pilot without vendor-specific concepts entering the Capability Plan.
measurements: Sorting, selection, row action, and detail disclosure coverage
License boundary for advanced data capabilities
findings: All candidates are assessed against the same twelve data-intensive capabilities.
MUI supplies the most direct native coverage but exposes a commercial detail-panel boundary.
Carbon supplies strong table, density, and accessibility coverage but RTL and virtualization remain unresolved.
Radix lacks first-party sorting, pagination, virtualization, and collection keyboard behavior.
React Aria and shadcn avoid paid blockers but require more Meridian-owned visual or composition work.
All five pinned implementations completed sort, selection, detail, pagination, focus restoration, RTL, forced-colors, and responsive automated journeys across the three required viewports.
The automated spike records candidate-specific build footprints, but manual assistive-technology and platform High Contrast evidence remains required.

unresolvedItems: The benchmark capability boundary is research-only until the M5 Capability Plan and Adapter contract are approved.
The isolated automated comparison is complete, but VoiceOver plus Chrome manual journeys are pending for both Pilots and every candidate.
Browser UI zoom at 200 percent and Windows High Contrast remain pending; CSS zoom and forced-colors emulation are supporting evidence only.
Dependency audit findings and candidate-specific bundle footprints must be included in the final weighted comparison.
No candidate may be recommended or selected from automated evidence alone.
revisitTriggers: Adapter capability coverage falls below the approved threshold
A non-React production target becomes a committed requirement
